newsitem.title: MEXICO: MEXICO CETES RATE UP, MARKET AWAITS U.S. DATA.
newsitem.headline: MEXICO CETES RATE UP, MARKET AWAITS U.S. DATA.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates were up 110 basis points at 19.60 percent in early trade on Monday, on what analysts said was caution ahead of the U.S. bond market's reaction to inflation data due later in the week.
"The market is trading at higher rates than on Friday as a preventative move in case of fallout from U.S. long bond yield in the wake of inflation data," a fixed-income analyst said.
Dealers noted the U.S. 30-year Treasury bond, off 9/32 to yield 6.66 percent, was also exerting pressure on secondary market rates in Mexico.
Overnight rates on bank paper shadowed government rates and were up 100 basis points at 21.25 percent.
Liquidity of 1.073 billion pesos was scheduled to return to the system from prior central bank participation.
